state.decision_rationale: Deferred pending giant-line, memory, latency, and citation benchmarks. Reopen when a hard byte cap or streaming renderer solves a measured failure rather than adding policy complexity speculatively.

provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Fixed-ish chunk sizes with terminators work, but for very large files the multi-chunk dance adds a little ceremony. An optional single-chunk if under N bytes rule or a streaming-friendly variant could be useful later.
feedback.normalized_claim: Measure whether the fixed 64-line strategy should become adaptive by byte size, file size, structure, or streaming needs.

current_behavior: Exact files are split at line boundaries into chunks of at most 64 source lines.
Files of 64 lines or fewer already emit as one chunk regardless of byte size.
Each chunk carries range, byte count, trust posture, deterministic terminator, and separator rule.
The renderer currently holds each decoded file and final packet text in memory.

proposal.summary: Evaluate chunk policies that bound both navigation cost and memory or streaming cost while preserving exact byte reconstruction.
candidate_changes: Compare current line-bound chunks with byte-capped, hybrid line-and-byte, and structure-aligned chunks.
Define a single-chunk threshold using both lines and bytes so extremely long lines remain bounded.
Prototype a streaming renderer and parser that do not materialize the whole packet or whole large files in memory.
Keep chunk policy explicit and versioned if it affects deterministic packet identity.
non_goals: Do not sacrifice exact reconstruction for convenient boundaries.
Do not call the current under-64-line behavior missing single-chunk support.
Do not change chunk policy without measuring citation and token effects.

questions: Is the target improvement model navigation, transport streaming, memory usage, or visual ceremony?
What maximum byte size protects against one-line generated payloads?
Should chunk boundaries align to symbols when doing so does not exceed hard limits?
Does changing chunk policy need to change packet semantic identity or only rendered identity?
risks: Adaptive policies can reduce deterministic cache stability.
Structure-aligned chunks depend on uneven analyzer support.
Byte caps can split multibyte UTF-8 or line-oriented citations unless carefully implemented.
More policy metadata can exceed the ceremony it removes.
evidence_needed: File-size and line-length distribution across representative repositories.
Memory and latency profiles for current and streaming implementations.
Model citation tests across fixed, byte-capped, and symbol-aligned chunks.
Exact round-trip fixtures containing giant lines and multibyte UTF-8.
